title: Zero-Downtime Schema Migrations: Safe Index Creation & Column Additions
realWorldScenario: A developer deploys a migration to add a non-null column with a default value and an index on a 40-million row `orders` table during peak traffic: `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN tracking_code VARCHAR(64) DEFAULT 'PENDING' NOT NULL; CREATE INDEX idx_orders_tracking ON orders(tracking_code);`. The entire API locks up and crashes.
questionStatement: Identify the lock types acquired by standard DDL commands. Why did this migration cause API downtime? Write the safe, zero-downtime PostgreSQL procedure to add a column with a default value, enforce NOT NULL, and build the index on a live high-traffic table.
expectedConcepts: SHARE lock of standard CREATE INDEX blocking all writes
Lock queue pileup: writes blocked by DDL, reads blocked by queued writes
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY using 2-pass table scan
NOT VALID check constraint followed by VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
Batch backfilling to prevent transaction lock exhaustion
hints: What lock does CREATE INDEX require versus CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY?
How does CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY avoid blocking writes?
Why should you validate check constraints in a separate statement?
